rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The narration says the Prophet told al-Abbas to hold Abu Sufyan at the valley pass until the Muslim troops had passed.
rows.anchor: فقال صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم للعباس انصرف يا عباس فاحبسه عند مضيق الوادي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Abbas stopped Abu Sufyan at the mountain pass; successive tribes passed, and the Prophet's armored green battalion followed.
rows.anchor: فحبسته عند خطم الجبل بمضيق الوادي ومرت عليه القبائل قبيلة قبيلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeing the Prophet's force, Abu Sufyan called his nephew's power immense; al-Abbas answered that it was prophethood, and Abu Sufyan agreed.
rows.anchor: لقد أصبح ملك ابن أخيك عظيما، فقلت ويحك إنها النبوة فقال نعم إذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hakim ibn Hizam and Budayl ibn Warqa accepted Islam and allegiance, then were sent to invite Quraysh and announce safe places of refuge.
rows.anchor: وجاء حكيم بن حزام وبديل بن ورقاء رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم وأسلما وبايعاه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet promised safety to anyone entering Abu Sufyan's or Hakim's house, or shutting his door and refraining from fighting.
rows.anchor: ومن أغلق بابه وكف يده فهو آمن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet sent al-Zubayr with the Muhajirun cavalry to plant the standard at al-Hajun and wait for him.
rows.anchor: بعث في أثرهما الزبير بن العوام وأمره على خيل المهاجرين وأمره أن يغرز رايته بأعلى مكة بالحجون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sa'd ibn Ubada led the Ansar vanguard; Khalid ibn al-Walid entered lower Mecca with converts from Quda'a and Sulaym and planted a standard.
rows.anchor: وبعث خالد بن الوليد فيمن كان أسلم من قضاعة وبني سليم وأمره أن يدخل أسفل مكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet ordered all troops to refrain from fighting unless attacked, while naming four men and two singers for execution.
rows.anchor: أن يكفوا أيديهم ولا يقاتلوا إلا من قاتلهم، وأمرهم بقتل أربعة نفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ali killed al-Huwayrith and one of the two singers; the other singer escaped.
rows.anchor: فقتل علي عليه السلام الحويرث بن نفيل وإحدى القينتين وأفلتت الأخرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Maqis ibn Dubaba was killed in the market, while Sa'id ibn Hurayth beat Ammar to Ibn Khatal and killed him at the Kaaba curtains.
rows.anchor: وقتل مقبس بن ضبابة في السوق، وأدرك ابن خطل وهو متعلق بأستار الكعبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Sufyan hurried to the Prophet, took hold of and kissed his stirrup, then raised Sa'd's threat about slaughter and captivity.
rows.anchor: وسعى أبو سفيان إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم وأخذ غرزه أي ركابه فقبله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet ordered Ali to retrieve the standard from Sa'd and enter gently with it; Ali complied.
rows.anchor: أدركه وخذ الراية منه وكن أنت الذي يدخل بها وأدخلها إدخالا رفيقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quraysh leaders sheltered in the Kaaba fearing execution; the Prophet proclaimed God's unity, fulfilled promise, and victory over the confederates.
rows.anchor: لا إله إلا الله وحده وحده أنجز وعده ونصر عبده وهزم الأحزاب وحده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet returned claims over property, privilege, and blood to his authority, while restoring Kaaba service and pilgrim water provision to their families.
rows.anchor: إلا سدانة الكعبة وسقاية الحاج فإنهما مردودتان إلى أهليهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mecca remained sacred: hunting and cutting its plants or trees were forbidden, and found property could be taken only by an announcer.
rows.anchor: لا يختلى خلاها، ولا يقطع شجرها ولا ينفر صيدها، ولا تحل لقطتها إلا لمنشد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After reproaching Quraysh for expulsion, harm, and fighting, the Prophet released them; they entered Islam, and their conquest captivity gave rise to the name al-tulaqa.
rows.anchor: فاذهبوا فأنتم الطلقاء فخرج القوم فكأنما أنشروا من القبور ودخلوا في الإسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn al-Ziba'ri came to the Prophet and embraced Islam, reciting a poem of repentance for opposing him and following Satan.
rows.anchor: وجاء ابن الزبعري إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم وأسلم وقال

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: On the conquest, the Prophet struck the 360 idols around the Kaaba with a staff and recited verses declaring truth's arrival and falsehood's defeat.
rows.anchor: دخل النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم يوم الفتح وحول البيت ثلاثمائة وستون صنما

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The Prophet had the idols removed before entering the Kaaba and condemned images of Abraham and Ishmael holding divining arrows.
rows.anchor: أبى أن يدخل البيت وفيه الآلهة فامر بها فاخرجت وصورة إبراهيم وإسماعيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conquest reports are numerous; al-Tabataba'i presents the preceding account as a summary and directs readers to histories and hadith collections for full detail.
rows.anchor: والروايات حول قصة الفتح كثيرة من أراد استقصاءها فعليه بكتب السير وجوامع الأخبار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Meccan sura threatens Abu Lahab, his deeds, and his wife with destruction and Hell.
rows.anchor: بيان وعيد شديد لأبي لهب بهلاك نفسه وعمله وبنار جهنم ولامرأته، والسورة مكية

rows.speaker: الجوهري
rows.claim: Al-Jawhari explains tabab as loss and destruction; al-Raghib adds enduring loss, while others gloss it as disappointment or total lack of good.
rows.anchor: التب والتباب هو الخسران والهلاك على ما ذكره الجوهري، ودوام الخسران على ما ذكره الراغب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hands stand for means of achieving aims; their ruin means failed deeds, especially Abu Lahab's efforts to extinguish prophethood, and his own lasting loss of felicity.
rows.anchor: وتباب يديه خسرانهما فيما تكتسبانه من عمل وإن شئت فقل بطلان أعماله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening may be a curse against Abu Lahab's self and deeds, or God's decree that he be ruined.
rows.anchor: دعاء عليه بهلاك نفسه وبطلان ما كان يأتيه من الأعمال لإطفاء نور النبوة أو قضاء منه تعالى بذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Lahab, the Prophet's uncle, was persistently hostile and abusive; after the first public invitation he told the Prophet to perish, and this sura answered him.
rows.anchor: كان شديد المعاداة للنبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم مصرا في تكذيبه مبالغا في إيذائه

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some say Abu Lahab was his given name despite its form as a kunya; other reported names are Abd al-Uzza and Abd Manaf.
rows.anchor: وذكر بعضهم أن أبا لهب اسمه وإن كان في صورة الكنية، وقيل اسمه عبد العزى وقيل عبد مناف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The kunya is preferable to his personal name because Abu Lahab mocks him as bound to Hell's flames; Abd al-Uzza was avoided because al-Uzza is an idol's name.
rows.anchor: في ذكره في الآية بكنيته لا باسمه أن في ذلك تهكما به لأن أبا لهب يشعر بالنسبة إلى لهب النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first ma is negative; the second is relative, meaning his deeds or their effects, or a verbal noun meaning what he earned. Neither wealth nor work saved him from ruin.
rows.anchor: ما الأولى نافية وما الثانية موصولة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Lahab will enter everlasting Hell; the indefinite wording of flame magnifies and terrifies.
rows.anchor: أي سيدخل نارا ذات لهب وهي نار جهنم الخالدة، وفي تنكير لهب تفخيم له وتهويل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His wife is included under the concealed subject of will enter; hammalata al-hatab is accusative as an epithet cut off for blame, or a circumstantial description.
rows.anchor: عطف على ضمير الفاعل المستكن في { سيصلى }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative parses hammalata al-hatab as a circumstantial description of his wife, which the author calls subtle and develops next.
rows.anchor: وقيل حال من { امرأته } وهو معنى لطيف على ما سيأتي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Masad is a rope twisted from palm fiber, and the clause is a second circumstantial description of Abu Lahab's wife.
rows.anchor: المسد حبل مفتول من الليف، والجملة حال ثانية من امرأته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verses depict her in Hell carrying the thorn branches she used to scatter at night on the Prophet's path, now punished with firewood and a fiber rope around her neck.
rows.anchor: كانت تحمل أغصان الشوك وغيرها تطرحها بالليل في طريق رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

rows.speaker: مجمع البيان
rows.claim: Al-Majma' asks whether Abu Lahab was still obligated to believe and could have done so without disproving the threat; it answers that faith remained obligatory and the threat was conditional on disbelief.
rows.anchor: فالجواب أن الإيمان يلزمه لأن تكليف الإيمان ثابت عليه وإنما توعده الله بشرط أن لا يؤمن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says God's decisive decree does not cancel choice: He wills human acts as voluntary, so Abu Lahab could choose faith and escape the punishment decreed for his unbelief.
rows.anchor: أن تعلق القضاء الحتمي منه تعالى بفعل الإنسان الاختياري لا يستوجب بطلان الاختيار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The same pattern applies to declarations that Quraysh disbelievers will not believe and to verses about hearts being sealed.
rows.anchor: ومن هذا الباب الآيات النازلة في كفار قريش أنهم لا يؤمنون

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: After the warning to nearest kin, the Prophet asked Quraysh whether they would believe a warning of imminent attack; when they affirmed, he warned them of punishment and Abu Lahab cursed him, prompting the sura.
rows.anchor: قال أبو لهب تبا لك ألهذا دعوتنا جميعا؟ فأنزل الله عز وجل

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Al-Tabataba'i says Sa'id ibn Jubayr also transmits the Ibn Abbas account in the sura commentary, without linking it to the nearest-kin verse.
rows.anchor: ورواه أيضا في تفسير السورة عن سعيد بن جبير عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: طارق المحاربي
rows.claim: At the Dhul-Majaz market, he saw Muhammad inviting people to profess God's unity while Abu Lahab followed, bleeding his legs and calling him a liar.
rows.anchor: إذا أنا بشاب يقول أيها الناس قولوا لا إله إلا الله تفلحوا، وإذا برجل خلفه يرميه

rows.speaker: موسى بن جعفر عليه السلام
rows.claim: When the sura was revealed, Umm Jamil approached angrily with a stone; the Prophet told Abu Bakr she could not see him, and said God had placed a barrier between them.
rows.anchor: أن أم جميل امرأه أبي لهب أتته حين نزلت سورة تبت ومع النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم أبو بكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Comparable versions of the Umm Jamil account occur through several Sunni chains.
rows.anchor: وروي ما يقرب منه بغير واحد من طرق أهل السنة

rows.speaker: تفسير القمي
rows.claim: Al-Qummi identifies the wife as Umm Jamil bint Sakhr and says she spread the Prophet's words among unbelievers.
rows.anchor: كانت أم جميل بنت صخر وكانت تنم على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم وتنقل أحاديثه إلى الكفار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sura describes God's unique essence and the dependence of everything else on Him in every existential need, without partner in essence, attributes, or acts; this grounds Quranic monotheism.
rows.anchor: تصفه تعالى بأحدية الذات ورجوع ما سواه إليه في جميع حوائجه الوجودية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reports on the sura's merit are abundant, including traditions from both communities that it equals one third of the Quran.
rows.anchor: وقد تكاثرت الأخبار في فضل السورة حتى ورد من طرق الفريقين أنها تعدل ثلث القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sura may be Meccan or Medinan, but reports about its occasion of revelation make a Meccan origin more apparent.
rows.anchor: والسورة تحتمل المكية والمدنية، والظاهر من بعض ما ورد في سبب نزولها أنها مكية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Huwa is a pronoun of the matter or story, drawing attention to the sentence that follows.
rows.anchor: هو ضمير الشأن والقصة يفيد الاهتمام بمضمون الجملة التالية له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Allah is a proper name for God by dominant usage in Arabic, as other languages also have a distinctive name for Him.
rows.anchor: الحق أن لفظ الجلالة علم بالغلبة له تعالى بالعربية كما أن له في غيرها من اللغات اسما خاصا به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ahad derives from unity but excludes plurality even in thought, unlike wahid, which admits a second or third by supposition; affirmative use is therefore reserved for God.
rows.anchor: إن الأحد إنما يطلق على ما لا يقبل الكثرة لا خارجا ولا ذهنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The contrast appears in negation: denying that any one came excludes one, while denying that any one of a group came excludes two or more as well.
rows.anchor: فإنك إنما تنفي به مجيء واحد منهم بالعدد ولا ينافيه مجيء اثنين منهم أو أكثر

rows.speaker: علي عليه أفضل السلام
rows.claim: Ali says every entity called one apart from God is only a little thing, illustrating God's incomparable unity.
rows.anchor: كل مسمى بالوحدة غيره قليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Samad derives from intending or seeking with reliance; reported definitions mostly mean the master whom needs are directed toward, and without qualification means the universal object of need.
rows.anchor: الأصل في معنى الصمد القصد أو القصد مع الاعتماد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because God originates every other existent, all things depend on Him in their essence, attributes, and effects; He is the endpoint of every need.
rows.anchor: فيقصده كل ما صدق عليه إنه شيء غيره، في ذاته وصفاته وآثاره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The definite article in al-Samad marks exclusivity: God alone is the absolute Samad, whereas ahad already excludes all others by its meaning.
rows.anchor: فهو تعالى وحده الصمد على الإطلاق، وهذا بخلاف احد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating Allah makes each clause independently sufficient to identify Him by an exclusive attribute.
rows.anchor: للإشارة إلى كون كل من الجملتين وحدها كافية في تعريفه تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ahad describes God's essence, while al-Samad describes His action as the endpoint of all things.
rows.anchor: والآيتان مع ذلك تصفانه تعالى بصفة الذات وصفة الفعل جميعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reported definition takes Samad to mean solid and non-hollow, needing no food, drink, sleep, offspring, or birth; then the next verse explains the word.
rows.anchor: وقيل الصمد بمعنى المصمت الذي ليس بأجوف فلا يأكل ولا يشرب ولا ينام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Not begetting denies partition or derivation from God, including Christian claims about Christ and pagan claims that deities are God's children.
rows.anchor: تنفيان عنه تعالى أن يلد شيئا بتجزيه في نفسه فينفصل عنه شيء سنخه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Not being born denies any origin or derivation from another, including pagan genealogies in which one deity is another's parent or child.
rows.anchor: وتنفيان عنه أن يكون متولدا من شيء آخر ومشتقا منه بأي معنى أريد من الاشتقاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No equal means none matches God in essence or in creating and governing; although no one posits another Necessary Being, idolaters claim delegated independent rule for beings such as Pharaoh and Nimrod.
rows.anchor: وأما الكفؤ في فعله وهو التدبير فقد قيل به كآلهة الوثنية من البشر كفرعون ونمرود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Any supposed independent action in a possible being implies self-sufficiency from God, which the verse denies because all beings need Him.
rows.anchor: فإنه كفاءة مرجعها استغناؤه عنه تعالى وهو محتاج من كل جهة والآية تنفيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Begetting entails composition and need, incompatible with the Samad to whom every needy thing turns.
rows.anchor: فإن الولادة التي هي نوع من التجزي والتبعض بأي معنى فسرت لا تخلو من تركيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Being born entails dependence for existence, incompatible with God's complete self-sufficiency.
rows.anchor: فإن تولد شيء من شيء لا يتم إلا مع حاجة من المتولد إلى ما ولد منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An equal would require independence and self-sufficiency, contradicting God's absolute Samadiyya and every creature's dependence on Him.
rows.anchor: لا تتحقق كفاءته إلا مع استقلاله واستغنائه عنه تعالى فيما فيه الكفاءة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The denials follow from God's Samadiyya and yield unity in essence, attributes, and acts; all other beings and their qualities exist through His giving. The sura summarizes Him as uniquely One.
rows.anchor: ومآل ما ذكر من صمديته تعالى وما يتفرع عليه إلى إثبات توحده تعالى في ذاته وصفاته وافعاله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some interpret kufuwan as a spouse and connect the verse with the declaration that God has taken no consort; the author dismisses this reading.
rows.anchor: ومما قيل في الآية أن المراد بالكفؤ الزوجة فإن زوجة الرجل كفؤه

rows.speaker: محمد بن مسلم
rows.claim: Abu Abdillah reports that Jews asked the Prophet to describe his Lord; after three days without a reply, the sura was revealed.
rows.anchor: إن اليهود سألوا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم فقالوا انسب لنا ربك فلبث ثلاثا لا يجيبهم

rows.speaker: العسكري عليه السلام
rows.claim: A report identifies the Jewish questioner as Abd Allah ibn Suriya; Sunni reports instead name Abd Allah ibn Salam, other Jews, or Meccan polytheists.
rows.anchor: أن السائل عبد الله بن صوريا اليهودي، وفي بعض روايات أهل السنة أن السائل عبد الله بن سلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Despite differing reports about the questioners, nasab here means description and attribute.
rows.anchor: وكيف كان فالمراد بالنسبة النعت والوصف

rows.speaker: الأصبغ بن نباتة
rows.claim: A report from Ali concerning God's description quotes the opening of the sura.
rows.anchor: عن الأصبغ بن نباتة عن علي عليه السلام في حديث نسبة الله عز وجل قل هو الله

rows.speaker: الصادق عليه السلام
rows.claim: In a report about the Ascension, God calls the sura His description and attribute; a similar report is also transmitted from Musa ibn Ja'far.
rows.anchor: اقرأ قل هو الله أحد كما انزلت فانها نسبتي ونعتي

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Abu Ubayd transmits from Ibn Abbas that the Prophet said the sura equals one third of the Quran; many reports give the same merit.
rows.anchor: قل هو الله أحد ثلث القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The strongest explanation is that Quranic teaching concerns unity, prophecy, and resurrection, and this sura contains one of those three foundations: unity.
rows.anchor: أعدلها أن ما في القرآن من المعارف تنحل إلى الأصول الثلاثة التوحيد والنبوة والمعاد

rows.speaker: أمير المؤمنين عليه السلام
rows.claim: Ali says Khidr taught him the invocation ya Hu before Badr; the Prophet identified it as the Greatest Name, which Ali kept on his tongue in battle.
rows.anchor: رأيت الخضر عليه السلام في المنام قبل بدر بليلة فقلت له علمني شيئا أنصر به على الأعداء

rows.speaker: أمير المؤمنين عليه السلام
rows.claim: After reciting the sura, Ali invoked God as ya Hu and asked forgiveness and victory over the unbelievers.
rows.anchor: وإن أمير المؤمنين عليه السلام قرأ قل هو الله أحد فلما فرغ قال يا هو يا من لا هو إلا هو

rows.speaker: علي عليه السلام
rows.claim: Ali's sermon defines ahad as not implying number; al-Rida also transmits this wording.
rows.anchor: الأحد لا بتأويل عدد

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر الثاني عليه السلام
rows.claim: Asked what al-Samad means, he answers: the master toward whom one turns in little and great matters.
rows.anchor: السيد المصمود إليه في القليل والكثير

rows.speaker: الباقر عليه السلام
rows.claim: Al-Baqir defines Samad as the master obeyed, with no commander or forbidding authority above Him.
rows.anchor: الصمد السيد المطاع الذي ليس فوقه آمر وناه

rows.speaker: الحسين عليه السلام
rows.claim: Al-Husayn's transmitted glosses include being without a cavity, not sleeping, ever-present, and creating forms and pairs while remaining unique without likeness or opposite.
rows.anchor: الصمد الذي لا جوف له والصمد الذي لا ينام، والصمد الذي لم يزل ولا يزال

rows.speaker: السجاد عليه السلام
rows.claim: Al-Sajjad describes Samad as the one who creates by command and originates contrasting forms and pairs while remaining singular without a counterpart.
rows.anchor: الصمد الذي إذا أراد شيئا قال له كن فيكون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root meaning reported from Abu Ja'far is primary; the other transmitted glosses follow as implications of all needs ultimately turning to God.
rows.anchor: والأصل في معنى الصمد هو الذي رويناه عن أبي جعفر الثاني عليه السلام

rows.speaker: الحسين عليه السلام
rows.claim: A report says people of Basra asked al-Husayn about Samad; he warns against speaking about the Quran without knowledge and cites the Prophet's threat of punishment.
rows.anchor: أما بعد فلا تخوضوا في القرآن ولا تجادلوا فيه ولا تتكلموا فيه بغير علم

rows.speaker: موسى بن جعفر عليه السلام
rows.claim: God is one, unique, and Samad: He neither begets and leaves an heir nor is born and shares existence with another.
rows.anchor: واعلم أن الله تعالى واحد أحد صمد لم يلد فيورث ولم يولد فيشارك

rows.speaker: علي عليه السلام
rows.claim: Ali's sermon says God was not born to share in glory and did not beget to become inherited or perish.
rows.anchor: الذي لم يولد فيكون في العز مشاركا ولم يلد فيكون موروثا هالكا

rows.speaker: علي عليه السلام
rows.claim: Another sermon declares God exalted above having an equal that resembles Him.
rows.anchor: تعالى أن يكون له كفؤ فيشبه به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sura commands the Prophet to seek refuge in God from every kind of evil and particular evils; reports make its Medinan origin apparent.
rows.anchor: أمر للنبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم أن يعوذ بالله من كل شر ومن بعضه خاصة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Falaq means splitting or cleaving and commonly denotes dawn split from darkness, an apt image for protection from evil that conceals good.
rows.anchor: والغالب إطلاقه على الصبح لأنه المشقوق من الظلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other readings take al-falaq as all that is brought forth by creation, or as a pit in Hell, the latter supported by some reports.
rows.anchor: وقيل المراد بالفلق كل ما يفطر ويفلق عنه بالخلق والإيجاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The evil sought against is evil carried by humans, jinn, animals, and other creatures; this does not imply evil in every created thing.
rows.anchor: من شر من يحمل شرا من الإنس والجن والحيوانات وسائر ما له شر من الخلق

rows.speaker: الصحاح
rows.claim: Al-Sihah defines ghasiq as the beginning darkness of night and also as night after twilight; wuqub means entering.
rows.anchor: الغسق أول ظلمة الليل وقد غسق الليل يغسق إذا أظلم والغاسق الليل إذا غاب الشفق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse seeks refuge from night as it darkens, since darkness helps evildoers conceal themselves and leaves people more vulnerable; another view means any harmful assailant.
rows.anchor: ومن شر الليل إذا دخل بظلمته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mentioning night after all creation is a special case after a general one, highlighting three common evils: darkness, sorcery, and envy.
rows.anchor: وذكر شر الليل إذا دخل بعد ذكر شر ما خلق من ذكر الخاص بعد العام لزيادة الاهتمام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Naffathat are women sorcerers who blow into knots, singled out because women practiced sorcery more often.
rows.anchor: أي النساء الساحرات اللاتي يسحرن بالعقد على المسحور وينفثن في العقد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse affirms that sorcery has some effect, as illustrated by the account of Harut and Marut.
rows.anchor: وفي الآية تصديق لتأثير السحر في الجملة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Harut and Marut account says people learned magic that could separate spouses, though it harmed no one without God's permission; Pharaoh's magicians offer a parallel.
rows.anchor: فيتعلمون منهما ما يفرقون به بين المرء وزوجه وما هم بضارين به من أحد إلا بإذن الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A distant interpretation treats the women as wives bending husbands' opinions to their own wishes, with knots as opinions and blowing as dissolving resolve.
rows.anchor: وقيل المراد بالنفاثات في العقد النساء اللاتي يملن آراء أزواجهن إلى ما يرينه ويردنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The envier's evil operates when envy takes hold and the person acts on it.
rows.anchor: إذا تلبس بالحسد وعمل بما في نفسه من الحسد بترتيب الأثر عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view includes the evil eye as a form of envy activated when someone sees what they find extraordinary or abundant.
rows.anchor: وقيل الآية تشمل العائن فعين العائن نوع حسد نفساني

rows.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
rows.claim: A Jewish man bewitched the Prophet, who fell ill; Gabriel directed Ali to retrieve the magic from a well and undo its knots while reciting verses, after which the Prophet recovered.
rows.anchor: سحر النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم رجل من اليهود فاشتكى فأتاه جبريل فنزل عليه بالمعوذتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Similar reports occur in Imami and Sunni sources with minor differences, including versions that send al-Zubayr and Ammar with Ali.
rows.anchor: وفي هذا المعنى روايات كثيرة من طرق أهل السنة باختلافات يسيرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet's protection from being called mentally bewitched does not prevent bodily illness from sorcery; no evidence establishes immunity from physical effects.
rows.anchor: وأما تأثره عن السحر بمرض يصيبه في بدنه ونحوه فلا دليل على مصونيته منه

rows.speaker: مجمع البيان
rows.claim: The Prophet often sought protection for al-Hasan and al-Husayn with these two suras.
rows.anchor: أن النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم كان كثيرا ما يعوذ الحسن والحسين عليهما السلام بهاتين السورتين

rows.speaker: عقبة بن عامر
rows.claim: The Prophet said these two protective suras were revealed to him without equal; al-Tabataba'i notes the report appears in sound sources.
rows.anchor: انزلت علي آيات لم ينزل مثلهن المعوذتان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The claim that none like them were revealed may mean that these two alone are dedicated to seeking refuge.
rows.anchor: ولعل المراد من عدم نزول مثلهن أنهما في العوذة فقط

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Reports from Ibn Abbas and Ibn Masud say Ibn Masud erased the two suras from the codex, arguing they were protective prayers rather than Quran, and did not recite them.
rows.anchor: كان يحك المعوذتين من المصحف ويقول لا تخلطوا القرآن بما ليس منه

rows.speaker: البزار
rows.claim: Al-Bazzar says no other Companion followed Ibn Masud; sound reports establish that the Prophet recited the suras in prayer and that they are in the codex.
rows.anchor: وقد صح عن النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم أنه قرأ بهما في الصلاة وقد أثبتتا في المصحف

rows.speaker: أبو بكر الحضرمي
rows.claim: Asked about Ibn Masud erasing them, Abu Ja'far says his father held that this was Ibn Masud's own opinion and that the two are Quranic suras.
rows.anchor: كان أبي يقول إنما فعل ذلك ابن مسعود برأيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Numerous reports from both communities and decisive mass transmission establish that the two suras are part of the Quran.
rows.anchor: على أن هناك تواترا قطعيا من عامة المنتحلين بالإسلام على كونهما من القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An objection from Ibn Masud's reported doubt about their Quranic status is answered by mass transmission; no report says he denied their revelation or miraculous eloquence.
rows.anchor: بل قال بعدم كونهما جزءا من القرآن وهو محجوج بالتواتر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sura commands refuge from the withdrawing whisperer; like al-Falaq, it is Medinan, and reports suggest both were revealed together.
rows.anchor: أمر للنبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم أن يعوذ من شر الوسواس الخناس والسورة مدنية كسابقتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A threatened person seeks refuge in a caretaker, a powerful sovereign, or a worshipped God; Allah uniquely combines all three grounds of protection.
rows.anchor: والذي يراه صالحا للعوذ والاعتصام به أحد ثلاثة إما رب يلي أمره ويدبره ويربيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God identifies Himself as humanity's Lord, King, and God, and the cited verses establish His lordship, sovereignty, and divinity as reasons to entrust oneself to Him.
rows.anchor: والله سبحانه رب الناس وملك الناس وإله الناس كما جمع الصفاة الثلاث لنفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is told to seek refuge in God because he too belongs to humankind and God is their Lord, King, and God.
rows.anchor: أمر لنبيه صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم أن يعوذ به لأنه من الناس وهو تعالى رب الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The order moves from the nearest and most particular guardian, to the more remote sovereign with wider authority, to God sought through exclusive devotion rather than material instinct.
rows.anchor: فذكر الرب أولا لأنه أقرب من الإنسان وأخص ولاية ثم الملك لأنه أبعد منالا وأعم ولاية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The three attributes are unjoined because each independently provides a reason to seek protection.
rows.anchor: وذلك للإشارة إلى كون كل من الصفات سببا مستقلا في دفع الشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeatedly naming each attribute instead of using a pronoun reinforces its independent sufficiency, as in the repeated Allah of the opening sura.
rows.anchor: وقد مر نظير الوجه في قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating people instead of saying their Lord or God shows that each attribute independently grounds refuge; other proposed explanations add nothing.
rows.anchor: ظهر أيضا وجه تكرار لفظ الناس من غير أن يقال ربهم وإلههم

rows.speaker: مجمع البيان
rows.claim: Al-Majma' defines waswas as an inner thought like a faint sound; it is likely an intensive descriptive use, though some call it an adjective rather than a verbal noun.
rows.anchor: الوسواس حديث النفس بما هو كالصوت الخفي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Waswas is an audible-form verbal noun of whispering, though the regular pattern would have kasra on its first waw.
rows.anchor: كالوسوسة كما ذكره وذكروا أنه سماعي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khannas intensively means one who withdraws after appearing; Satan whispers, retreats when God is remembered, and returns when people forget.
rows.anchor: الخناس صيغة مبالغة من الخنوس بمعنى الاختفاء بعد الظهور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The relative clause describes the whisperer; breasts mean souls, since perception begins in the self and is conventionally associated with the heart in the chest.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالصدور هي النفوس لأن متعلق الوسوسة هو مبدأ الإدراك من الإنسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jinn and people explain the whisperer's sources, indicating that some humans join the devils' ranks.
rows.anchor: وفيه إشارة إلى أن من الناس من هو ملحق بالشياطين وفي زمرتهم

rows.speaker: أبو خديجة
rows.claim: Gabriel visited the sick Prophet and recited al-Mu'awwidhatayn and al-Ikhlas as a healing protection from every painful illness.
rows.anchor: جاء جبرئيل إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم وهو شاك فرقاه بالمعوذتين وقل هو الله أحد

rows.speaker: أنس بن مالك
rows.claim: The Prophet says Satan places his snout on a person's heart, withdraws when God is remembered, and fastens on again when He is forgotten.
rows.anchor: إن الشيطان واضع خطمه على قلب ابن آدم فإذا ذكر الله خنس

rows.speaker: أبان بن تغلب
rows.claim: Ja'far ibn Muhammad says every believer has two heart-ears: an angel whispers into one and the withdrawing whisperer into the other, while God supports the believer through the angel.
rows.anchor: ما من مؤمن إلا ولقلبه في صدره أذنان أذن ينفث فيها الملك وأذن ينفث فيها الوسواس الخناس

rows.speaker: الصادق عليه السلام
rows.claim: After the verse on remembering God and seeking forgiveness, Satan convenes his demons; the withdrawing whisperer wins appointment by promising temptation and making sinners forget repentance.
rows.anchor: أعدهم وأمنيهم حتى يواقعوا الخطيئة فإذا واقعوا الخطيئة أنسيتهم الاستغفار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The book has discussed Satan earlier in its eighth volume.
rows.anchor: تقدم بعض الكلام في الشيطان في أوائل الجزء الثامن من الكتاب
